summary: Second Candidate on the accepted v1 map, action=continue, created from a lead the map itself surfaced. It investigates F-log-persisted (lifecycle preservation) established by B-follower-append and consumed by B-quorum-commit, with A1 relationship and A2 context support (B-election consuming the same cached last entry; B-authority-loss as the surrounding transition). The sourced discrepancy is in hashicorp/raft's appendEntries error paths: after a conflicting suffix is truncated by DeleteRange, a subsequent StoreLogs failure returns with Success=false while raftState.lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm still name the truncated suffix - the code itself flags this with the comment 'TODO: leaving r.getLastLog() in the wrong state if there was a truncation above' (raft.go:1541) - and a second early return after a successful StoreLogs (processConfigurationLogEntry error at raft.go:1547-1553) also skips setLastLog. The question asks whether the cached last log identity stays consistent with what the LogStore actually holds and, if not, whether the divergence can change a safety-relevant decision (AppendEntriesResponse.LastLog feeding the leader's nextIndex retry; the RequestVote up-to-date check via r.getLastEntry()) or only availability. Counterevidence records that both paths answer Success=false, that later successful stores overwrite the cache, and that reachability needs a store failing after DeleteRange; the remaining unknowns fix the discriminator (reachability of the truncation-then-failure path, safety vs availability consequence, and whether restart repairs the divergence). Cites acquired Materials (S-raft-appendentries, S-logstore, S-commitment, S-updatelastappended, S-replication, S-raft-requestvote). Preflight valid:true; no defect is presumed.
